## tests/ngv2/test_targets_scanner_wired.py
```python
"""Hermetic oracle: each of the 5 e2e PoC targets scans as EXACTLY its own
pattern id (and no foreign id) via the real ``pattern_scanner.scan_directory``.

TARGETS_ROOT resolution: an env var ``D5POC_TARGETS_ROOT`` overrides; otherwise
the module-level default points at the development location under /tmp. When
these files move into NGv2, repoint the default to ``_e2e_run/targets`` (i.e.
``Path(ngv2_repo_root) / "_e2e_run" / "targets"``).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from ngv2.pattern_scanner import scan_directory

# Self-locating: this oracle lives at <repo>/tests/ngv2/, so the targets are at
# <repo>/_e2e_run/targets. An env var override is still honored.
_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
TARGETS_ROOT = Path(
    os.environ.get("D5POC_TARGETS_ROOT", str(_REPO_ROOT / "_e2e_run" / "targets"))
)

# pattern id -> expected CWE (sanity-cross-checks the scanner catalog).
EXPECTED = {
    "command_injection": "CWE-78",
    "eval_usage": "CWE-95",
    "sql_injection": "CWE-89",
    "hardcoded_secret": "CWE-798",
    "weak_crypto": "CWE-327",
}


@pytest.mark.parametrize("pattern,cwe", sorted(EXPECTED.items()))
def test_target_scans_as_exactly_its_pattern(pattern: str, cwe: str) -> None:
    target_dir = TARGETS_ROOT / pattern
    assert target_dir.is_dir(), f"missing target dir: {target_dir}"

    report = scan_directory(str(target_dir))
    assert "error" not in report, report
    assert report["total_findings"] >= 1, f"no findings for {pattern}: {report}"

    ids = {f["id"] for f in report["findings"]}
    assert pattern in ids, f"{pattern} not detected; got {sorted(ids)}"

    foreign = sorted(i for i in ids if i != pattern)
    assert not foreign, f"{pattern} target tripped foreign patterns: {foreign}"

    cwes = {f["cwe"] for f in report["findings"]}
    assert cwes == {cwe}, f"{pattern} cwe mismatch: expected {{{cwe}}}, got {cwes}"

```

```python
"""RED oracle: wire ngv2/deser_detect.py (CWE-502) into the live scan catalog.

Contract (from brief_hooks_learning-selection-layer): the scan catalog is
``ngv2.pattern_scanner.VULN_PATTERNS``. The EDIT registers a deserialization
entry so the live scan path emits CWE-502 findings:

* ``VULN_PATTERNS`` gains an entry whose ``cwe`` is ``'CWE-502'`` for the
  ``python`` language, with severity ``'critical'``, whose pattern mirrors the
  ``ngv2.deser_detect.DESER_PATTERNS`` usage sinks (pickle/marshal/yaml.load/
  torch.load/joblib.load style calls).
* ``scan_file`` / ``scan_directory`` flag ``pickle.loads(`` and ``torch.load(``
  lines in Python sources with a CWE-502 finding.
* ``ngv2.deser_detect`` itself is NOT modified: ``check_deserialization`` and
  ``DESER_PATTERNS`` keep their existing behavior (regression-pinned below).
* Existing catalog entries are untouched (command_injection still fires).
"""
from ngv2.deser_detect import DESER_PATTERNS, check_deserialization
from ngv2.pattern_scanner import VULN_PATTERNS, scan_file


def _cwe502_entries():
    return {
        ident: meta
        for ident, meta in VULN_PATTERNS.items()
        if meta.get("cwe") == "CWE-502"
    }


def test_catalog_gains_cwe_502_entry():
    entries = _cwe502_entries()
    assert entries, "VULN_PATTERNS has no CWE-502 entry"
    for meta in entries.values():
        assert "python" in meta["languages"]
        assert meta["severity"] == "critical"


def test_scan_file_flags_pickle_and_torch_sinks(tmp_path):
    target = tmp_path / "vuln.py"
    target.write_text(
        "import pickle\n"
        "def load(blob):\n"
        "    return pickle.loads(blob)\n"
        "def load_model(path):\n"
        "    import torch\n"
        "    return torch.load(path)\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    findings = scan_file(target, "python")
    cwes = {f["cwe"] for f in findings}
    assert "CWE-502" in cwes
    lines = {f["line"] for f in findings if f["cwe"] == "CWE-502"}
    assert 3 in lines  # pickle.loads
    assert 6 in lines  # torch.load


# edge_case: comment-only deser mention does not fire (catalog comment filter)
def test_commented_sink_not_flagged(tmp_path):
    target = tmp_path / "ok.py"
    target.write_text("# pickle.loads is dangerous\nx = 1\n", encoding="utf-8")
    assert all(f["cwe"] != "CWE-502" for f in scan_file(target, "python"))


# edge_case: existing catalog entries are untouched by the registration
def test_existing_entries_unchanged(tmp_path):
    assert "command_injection" in VULN_PATTERNS
    assert VULN_PATTERNS["command_injection"]["cwe"] == "CWE-78"
    target = tmp_path / "cmd.py"
    target.write_text("import os\nos.system(user_input)\n", encoding="utf-8")
    assert any(f["cwe"] == "CWE-78" for f in scan_file(target, "python"))


def test_deser_detect_itself_unchanged(tmp_path):
    # regression pin: deser_detect keeps its standalone behavior
    labels = [label for label, _ in DESER_PATTERNS]
    assert "pickle" in labels and "torch.load" in labels
    repo = tmp_path / "repo"
    repo.mkdir()
    (repo / "m.py").write_text("import pickle\nd = pickle.loads(b)\n", encoding="utf-8")
    report = check_deserialization(str(repo))
    assert report["has_deserialization"] is True
    assert report["total_matches"] >= 2
```

## tests/test_pattern_scanner.py
```python
"""RED oracle for ngv2.pattern_scanner — the deterministic regex-based
vulnerability pattern scanner.

Pure stdlib (``re``/``os``/``pathlib``). No semgrep, no network, no LLM. The
scanner reads source files from disk and emits structured finding dicts by
matching a curated ``VULN_PATTERNS`` catalog line-by-line, filtered by the
file's language (derived from ``LANG_EXTENSIONS``). ``scan_directory`` walks a
repo, skips ignored/test directories, dedups, and returns an aggregate report.

This oracle pins the exact public surface and return shapes. It does NOT pin
the full legacy 42-pattern catalog; it requires a stable *subset* of well-known
pattern ids to exist with the correct metadata schema, so the catalog can grow
without breaking the contract.
"""
from pathlib import Path

from ngv2.pattern_scanner import (
    scan_file,
    scan_directory,
    VULN_PATTERNS,
    LANG_EXTENSIONS,
)


# --- Required metadata schema for every VULN_PATTERNS entry ---
PATTERN_META_KEYS = {"pattern", "severity", "cwe", "owasp", "languages", "description"}

# --- Required finding dict shape emitted by scan_file ---
FINDING_KEYS = {"id", "file", "line", "code", "severity", "cwe", "owasp", "description"}

# --- A stable subset of pattern ids that MUST exist (catalog may have more) ---
REQUIRED_PATTERN_IDS = {
    "sql_injection",
    "command_injection",
    "eval_usage",
    "weak_crypto",
    "hardcoded_secret",
}

VALID_SEVERITIES = {"low", "medium", "high", "critical"}


def test_lang_extensions_maps_known_suffixes():
    # Suffixes are lowercase dotted keys -> language name strings.
    assert LANG_EXTENSIONS[".py"] == "python"
    assert LANG_EXTENSIONS[".js"] == "javascript"
    assert LANG_EXTENSIONS[".ts"] == "typescript"
    for ext, lang in LANG_EXTENSIONS.items():
        assert ext.startswith(".") and ext == ext.lower()
        assert isinstance(lang, str) and lang


def test_vuln_patterns_schema_is_complete():
    assert REQUIRED_PATTERN_IDS.issubset(set(VULN_PATTERNS))
    for vuln_id, meta in VULN_PATTERNS.items():
        assert isinstance(vuln_id, str) and vuln_id
        # Each entry exposes at least the required metadata keys.
        assert PATTERN_META_KEYS.issubset(set(meta)), vuln_id
        assert isinstance(meta["pattern"], str) and meta["pattern"]
        assert meta["severity"] in VALID_SEVERITIES, vuln_id
        assert meta["cwe"].startswith("CWE-"), vuln_id
        assert isinstance(meta["owasp"], str) and meta["owasp"]
        assert isinstance(meta["languages"], list) and meta["languages"]
        assert all(isinstance(x, str) for x in meta["languages"])
        assert isinstance(meta["description"], str) and meta["description"]


def test_scan_file_detects_python_sqli(tmp_path):
    p = tmp_path / "vuln.py"
    p.write_text('cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = %s" % uid)\n')
    findings = scan_file(p, "python")
    ids = {f["id"] for f in findings}
    assert "sql_injection" in ids
    f = next(f for f in findings if f["id"] == "sql_injection")
    # Exact finding shape.
    assert set(f) == FINDING_KEYS
    assert f["line"] == 1
    assert f["severity"] == VULN_PATTERNS["sql_injection"]["severity"]
    assert f["cwe"] == VULN_PATTERNS["sql_injection"]["cwe"]
    assert f["owasp"] == VULN_PATTERNS["sql_injection"]["owasp"]
    assert f["description"] == VULN_PATTERNS["sql_injection"]["description"]
    assert f["file"] == str(p)
    # code is the stripped source line.
    assert f["code"] == 'cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = %s" % uid)'


def test_scan_file_reports_correct_line_numbers(tmp_path):
    p = tmp_path / "m.py"
    p.write_text(
        "import os\n"
        "x = 1\n"
        "eval(user_input)\n"
    )
    findings = scan_file(p, "python")
    evals = [f for f in findings if f["id"] == "eval_usage"]
    assert evals, "expected eval_usage finding"
    assert evals[0]["line"] == 3  # 1-based line numbering


def test_scan_file_skips_comment_lines(tmp_path):
    p = tmp_path / "c.py"
    p.write_text(
        "# eval(user_input) -- this is a commented-out example\n"
        "eval(user_input)\n"
    )
    findings = scan_file(p, "python")
    eval_lines = sorted(f["line"] for f in findings if f["id"] == "eval_usage")
    # Only the real (line 2) hit; the commented line 1 is ignored.
    assert eval_lines == [2]


def test_scan_file_filters_by_language(tmp_path):
    # A Python-only pattern must not fire when the file is scanned as a
    # language not in that pattern's languages list.
    src = "import hashlib\nh = hashlib.md5(data)\n"
    py = tmp_path / "a.py"
    py.write_text(src)
    py_ids = {f["id"] for f in scan_file(py, "python")}
    assert "weak_crypto" in py_ids
    # Same bytes scanned as 'go' (weak_crypto's languages excludes go) -> no hit.
    go = tmp_path / "a.go"
    go.write_text(src)
    assert "weak_crypto" not in {f["id"] for f in scan_file(go, "go")}


def test_scan_file_clean_source_has_no_findings(tmp_path):
    p = tmp_path / "ok.py"
    p.write_text("def add(a, b):\n    return a + b\n")
    assert scan_file(p, "python") == []


def test_scan_file_missing_file_returns_empty_list(tmp_path):
    # Robust shell: unreadable/missing files yield [] (never raises).
    assert scan_file(tmp_path / "does_not_exist.py", "python") == []


def test_scan_directory_aggregate_report_shape(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / "app.py").write_text("eval(user_input)\n")
    (tmp_path / "lib.js").write_text("var h = crypto.createHash('md5');\n")
    report = scan_directory(str(tmp_path))
    # Required top-level report keys.
    for key in ("files_scanned", "total_findings", "severity_counts", "findings"):
        assert key in report, key
    assert isinstance(report["findings"], list)
    assert report["total_findings"] == len(report["findings"])
    assert report["files_scanned"] >= 2
    # Each finding still matches the per-finding schema; file path is repo-relative.
    for f in report["findings"]:
        assert set(f) == FINDING_KEYS
        assert not Path(f["file"]).is_absolute()
    # severity_counts sums to total_findings.
    assert sum(report["severity_counts"].values()) == report["total_findings"]


def test_scan_directory_skips_tests_by_default_and_includes_when_asked(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / "app.py").write_text("eval(user_input)\n")
    tdir = tmp_path / "tests"
    tdir.mkdir()
    (tdir / "test_app.py").write_text("eval(user_input)\n")

    default = scan_directory(str(tmp_path))
    default_files = {f["file"] for f in default["findings"]}
    assert not any("test" in fp for fp in default_files)

    with_tests = scan_directory(str(tmp_path), include_tests=True)
    with_files = {f["file"] for f in with_tests["findings"]}
    assert any("test" in fp for fp in with_files)
    assert with_tests["total_findings"] > default["total_findings"]


def test_scan_directory_missing_path_returns_error(tmp_path):
    report = scan_directory(str(tmp_path / "nope"))
    assert "error" in report


def test_scan_directory_dedups_identical_findings(tmp_path):
    # Same (id, file, line) must appear at most once.
    (tmp_path / "d.py").write_text("eval(a); eval(b)\n")
    report = scan_directory(str(tmp_path))
    keys = [(f["id"], f["file"], f["line"]) for f in report["findings"]]
    assert len(keys) == len(set(keys))

```

```python
"""Wired RED oracle for ngv2/novelty_corpus.py (Phase 7.2c: seed the novelty
corpus from prior accepted submissions).

The legacy feed to ngv2.novelty_gate.classify_novelty was ``[]`` so EVERYTHING
was NOVEL. This loader reads data/ngv2/huntr_existing_submissions.json — shaped
``{repo: {status, count, titles: [...]}}`` — and flattens it into the
``[{'title','cwe','file'}]`` entries classify_novelty expects, so a known prior
submission is no longer classified NOVEL.

Pinned contract:

- ``corpus_from_submissions_map(data)`` flattens a ``{repo: {titles: [...]}}``
  mapping into a list of dicts each having keys ``title``, ``cwe``, ``file`` (the
  repo, so same-repo locus hints survive). Malformed shapes are skipped, never
  raised.
- ``load_known_corpus(path=None)`` reads JSON from ``path`` (defaulting to the
  real data file) and returns the flattened corpus; missing/unparseable file
  returns ``[]`` (never raises).
- Round-trip: a title drawn from the loaded corpus, classified back through
  classify_novelty against that corpus, is NOT 'NOVEL'.
- Pure stdlib (json only); no network/clock/randomness. Path is injectable.
"""
import json

import pytest

from ngv2.novelty_corpus import (
    corpus_from_submissions_map,
    load_known_corpus,
    DEFAULT_CORPUS_PATH,
)
from ngv2.novelty_gate import classify_novelty


def test_flatten_shape_has_title_cwe_file():
    data = {"acme/x": {"titles": ["SSRF in fetch handler", "XSS in form"]}}
    c = corpus_from_submissions_map(data)
    assert len(c) == 2
    assert {"title", "cwe", "file"} <= set(c[0])
    assert c[0]["title"] == "SSRF in fetch handler"
    assert c[0]["file"] == "acme/x"


def test_flatten_skips_malformed_entries():
    data = {
        "ok/repo": {"titles": ["good title"]},
        "bad1": {"titles": "not-a-list"},
        "bad2": "not-a-dict",
        "bad3": {"no_titles": True},
        "bad4": {"titles": [123, None, "real"]},
    }
    c = corpus_from_submissions_map(data)
    titles = {e["title"] for e in c}
    assert "good title" in titles
    assert "real" in titles
    assert all(isinstance(e["title"], str) for e in c)


def test_non_dict_input_returns_empty():
    assert corpus_from_submissions_map(None) == []
    assert corpus_from_submissions_map([1, 2, 3]) == []


def test_load_missing_path_returns_empty(tmp_path):
    assert load_known_corpus(tmp_path / "nope.json") == []


def test_load_unparseable_returns_empty(tmp_path):
    p = tmp_path / "bad.json"
    p.write_text("{ not json", encoding="utf-8")
    assert load_known_corpus(p) == []


def test_loaded_corpus_makes_known_submission_not_novel(tmp_path):
    p = tmp_path / "subs.json"
    p.write_text(json.dumps(
        {"acme/x": {"status": 200, "count": 1,
                    "titles": ["SSRF in fetch handler"]}}),
        encoding="utf-8")
    corpus = load_known_corpus(p)
    finding = {"title": "SSRF in fetch handler", "cwe": "", "file": "acme/x"}
    assert classify_novelty(finding, corpus) != "NOVEL"


def test_default_path_points_at_real_data_file():
    # The default corpus is the real prior-submissions data file.
    assert DEFAULT_CORPUS_PATH.name == "huntr_existing_submissions.json"
    if DEFAULT_CORPUS_PATH.exists():
        corpus = load_known_corpus()
        assert len(corpus) > 0
        sample = corpus[0]
        finding = {"title": sample["title"], "cwe": sample["cwe"],
                   "file": sample["file"]}
        assert classify_novelty(finding, corpus) != "NOVEL"

```

## tests/test_novelty_corpus_cwe.py

```python
"""RED oracle: additive CWE fix in ngv2/novelty_corpus.py.

Contract (from brief_hooks_title-cwe-and-corpus-stats): where
``corpus_from_submissions_map`` / ``load_known_corpus`` currently flatten every
title with ``'cwe': ''``, the ``cwe`` field must instead be populated via
``ngv2.title_cwe_classifier.classify_title`` so the per-finding class signal is
preserved. Everything else stays behavior-compatible: entry shape
``{'title', 'cwe', 'file', 'repo'}``, malformed shapes skipped (never raised),
missing/unparseable file -> [].
"""
import json

from ngv2.novelty_corpus import corpus_from_submissions_map, load_known_corpus


def test_classifiable_title_gets_cwe_populated():
    data = {"beta/two": {"titles": ["Unsafe pickle deserialization in loader"]}}
    entries = corpus_from_submissions_map(data)
    assert len(entries) == 1
    assert entries[0]["cwe"] == "CWE-502"
    # behavior-compatible remainder of the entry shape
    assert entries[0]["title"] == "Unsafe pickle deserialization in loader"
    assert entries[0]["file"] == "beta/two"
    assert entries[0]["repo"] == "beta/two"


def test_command_injection_title_gets_cwe_78():
    data = {"alpha/one": {"titles": ["OS Command Injection in runner"]}}
    entries = corpus_from_submissions_map(data)
    assert entries[0]["cwe"] == "CWE-78"


# edge_case: unclassifiable title keeps cwe == '' (no false-positive class)
def test_unclassifiable_title_keeps_empty_cwe():
    data = {"alpha/one": {"titles": ["Bump dependency versions in changelog"]}}
    entries = corpus_from_submissions_map(data)
    assert entries[0]["cwe"] == ""


# edge_case: malformed shapes are still skipped, never raised
def test_malformed_shapes_still_skipped():
    data = {
        "ok/repo": {"titles": ["Path Traversal in download"]},
        "bad/repo1": "not-a-dict",
        "bad/repo2": {"titles": "not-a-list"},
        "bad/repo3": {"titles": [42, None]},
    }
    entries = corpus_from_submissions_map(data)
    assert [e["repo"] for e in entries] == ["ok/repo"]
    assert entries[0]["cwe"] == "CWE-22"


def test_load_known_corpus_populates_cwe(tmp_path):
    p = tmp_path / "subs.json"
    p.write_text(
        json.dumps({"r/x": {"status": 200, "count": 1, "titles": ["SSRF via unvalidated redirect URL"]}}),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    entries = load_known_corpus(p)
    assert len(entries) == 1
    assert entries[0]["cwe"] == "CWE-918"


def test_load_known_corpus_missing_file_still_empty(tmp_path):
    assert load_known_corpus(tmp_path / "nope.json") == []
```
